newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia appoints new mining official.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia appoints new mining official.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister on Monday appointed a new secretary-general for the ministry, replacing the man who played a prominent role in the Busang gold saga.
Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus named Darmoko Slamet as the new ministry secretary-general, replacing Umar Said.
Sudjana said Said's services were terminated honourably and that the move was not linked to the Busang scandal.
"The changing of officials in the organisation is routine," Sudjana said at the brief appointment ceremony.
"There is no link with the Busang case," he added.
Darmoko was previously president-director of state-owned mining company PT Aneka Tambang.
According to a statement issued by the ministry, Said's next position was still being decided by the government.
"I feel very relieved and relaxed," Said told reporters after the ceremony.

The Busang property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province had once been estimated by Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd to contain some 71 million ounces of gold, which would have made it the biggest gold find this century.

But an independent audit found insignificant amounts of gold at Busang. Consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd, which did the audit, also said data on the find had been falsified on an unprecedented scale.
Indonesian police and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating the scandal, the biggest mining fraud in history.
Sudjana last month appointed Adjat Sudradjat as director-general of mining, replacing Kuntoro Mangkusubroto.
Kuntoro also played a promiment role in the Busang saga.
